$policy: See docs/design/execution/chunk-0a/anchors.md §3.3 and docs/design/execution/chunk-0a/brief.md §3.3 (R12 / plan §15 rule 5). Every file under tests/fixtures/goldens/** (excluding this registry itself and fixture-refs.ts modules) must have exactly one entry below. designation is one of: "frozen-migration-input" (the asset is a preservation oracle — a chunk that touches its surface must reproduce it byte-for-byte/outcome-for-outcome; never re-recorded outside its owning chunk) or "re-baseline" (the asset deliberately baselines behavior a later chunk is going to change on purpose; reBaselineChunk names the manifest chunk id — see tests/fixtures/akm-0.9.0-chunk-manifest.json — where it is reviewed and re-captured). reBaselineChunk is required iff designation is "re-baseline" and must be absent otherwise. consumers[] lists the suite(s) that load the fixture via tests/_helpers/golden.ts's expectGolden/loadGolden. Policed by tests/goldens-designations.test.ts. | Amendment (2026-07-16 gate hardening): (1) every frozen-migration-input entry carries a sha256 of its asset bytes, verified by scripts/lint-goldens-presence.ts on every lint run — AKM_UPDATE_GOLDENS=1 cannot silently mutate a frozen oracle; a legitimate re-baseline updates designation+reBaselineChunk+sha256-removal in the same reviewed change. (2) Surface-owner rule: a chunk that the plan orders to change an asset's pinned surface becomes that asset's re-baseline owner — re-designate the entry (designation, reBaselineChunk, notes) BEFORE the surface change lands, so the re-capture is a reviewed diff, not a frozen-asset violation.

entries.notes: WI-03, plan §11 Chunk 0a / R3 (engines 1+2 of 3: proposal accept/revert + reject). Preservation oracle through Chunk 6's collapse into one FileChange transaction. Pins accept (new-asset, overwrite-with-backup, idempotent re-accept short-circuit, target-mutated-during-displace abort), revert (success restore, refuse-clobber), reject (success, non-pending UsageError, concurrent-edit succeeds -- reject has NO before-hash), as file-tree/DB-status/exactly-once-event outcomes only -- no journal bytes or paths (brief §3.2 rule 4). Contains fixture-local names only (tests/fixtures/goldens/journal/fixture-refs.ts) — no production refs. Caveat: the `fileTree` object's keys are relative asset paths (e.g. `lessons/<fixture-local-name>.md`) that embed the same fixture-local name a ref would carry; if Chunk 5's §15.2 ref-grammar codemod changes how names map to on-disk paths, these path keys (not the outcome booleans/counts) would need re-baselining alongside that migration even though this asset is otherwise designated frozen. Also records a captured DEVIATION from the brief's testsFirst description for the target-mutated-during-displace scenario (see the suite's file-header comment): the real surfaced abort error is 'Cannot roll back proposal transaction: <path> diverged.', not 'Proposal target changed while its backup was being acquired.', and the target is left holding the mutator's content rather than being byte-identically restored. | Split 2026-07-16 (surface-owner rule, pre-WI-6.4): the createProposal dedup/cooldown/force skip-record shapes moved to tests/fixtures/goldens/journal/proposal-skip-shapes.json (re-baseline @6) because the §23.6 fingerprint scheme legitimately changes them; the accept/revert/reject outcome scenarios in THIS asset stay frozen through the engine swap. sha256 re-pinned over the trimmed bytes in the same reviewed change. | RE-CAPTURED 2026-07-30 (#730, D2 — OKF v0.2 provenance stamping surface owner): promoteProposal now stamps OKF v0.2 provenance onto every accepted markdown asset in the HYBRID on-disk shape settled by the #730 review — bare top-level `generated:`/`verified:` (OKF's own spelling, so third-party OKF v0.2 readers see conformant trust metadata) with only `sources` namespaced under `provenance:` (a bare `sources:` collides with the wiki citation-string convention); re-recorded 2026-07-30 when the shape changed from fully-nested to hybrid, so the two fileTree SHA256 entries for the new-asset and overwrite-existing accept scenarios legitimately changed (added bytes); every other recorded outcome (status/backup/event counts/journal cleanup) is byte-for-byte unchanged, confirming the re-baseline is scoped to exactly the new feature's effect. The golden-capturing calls for those two scenarios now pin `ctx: {now, actorId}` (a new ProposalsContext seam) so the embedded `generatedAt`/`verified[].at` timestamp and the `human:<actorId>` fallback stay reproducible across machines/runs — without that pin the hash would depend on wall-clock time and the real OS username. Also note: `generated.by`/`verified.by` for these `distill`-sourced (automated) proposals is `akm/<pkgVersion>`, so a FUTURE package version bump will shift these two fileTree hashes again — an inherent, expected consequence of embedding the version into accepted content, not a defect. | RE-RECORDED (driver-side workflow-test port, this branch): the two fileTree SHA256 entries (lessons/jnl-accept-new-asset.md, lessons/jnl-accept-overwrite.md) shifted again -- diagnosed and confirmed NOT a regression: package.json's version bumped 0.9.0-rc.11 -> 0.9.0-rc.12 (commit 63c803b7, "chore: bump version to 0.9.0-rc.12") between this asset's last capture and this branch's HEAD, and `pkgVersion` (src/version.ts) reads package.json live at runtime, so the `akm/<pkgVersion>` embedded into `generated.by`/`verified[].by` for these two distill-sourced (automated) scenarios changed with it -- exactly the drift this entry's own prior note already predicted ("a FUTURE package version bump will shift these two fileTree hashes again -- an inherent, expected consequence of embedding the version into accepted content, not a defect"). Confirmed empirically: temporarily reverting ONLY package.json's version string to 0.9.0-rc.11 made the captured fileTree hashes match the pre-existing committed golden byte-for-byte; restoring the real 0.9.0-rc.12 and re-capturing reproduces exactly this diff, nothing else. The same-day #730 promotion-path re-validation fallback deletion (commit 957bdfd5, "refactor(workflow): delete content-sniffing and the closed allowlist") was investigated and ruled OUT as a contributing cause for this asset: that fallback only changes behavior when the per-type validator REJECTS the stamped candidate (falling back to unstamped content); the lesson type's stamped candidate already validated successfully at this asset's prior capture (0e13e289, whose own note records the fileTree hashes "legitimately changed (added bytes)" moving TO the stamped shape), so the fallback was never exercised for lesson and its deletion is behaviorally inert here.
